CalculateVars.maps_to: ThisOrThat.cs:23-26 sets Gold.BaseValue = base.Rng.NextInt(41, 69). events/this_or_that.py:28-29 `self._gold = self.rng.randint(41, 68)`. Rng.NextInt(minInclusive, maxExclusive) is exclusive on the top (Rng.cs:101-109) and Python's randint is inclusive on both, so 41..68 is the same 28-value range, drawn with one call. The STREAM it is drawn from is wrong -- see the EV-3 entry.

guards.what: EV-1: Plain (ThisOrThat.cs:39) deals DynamicVars.HpLoss = 6 through CreatureCmd.Damage with ValueProp.Unblockable | Unpowered can reduce the player to 0 HP. C# routes event damage through CreatureCmd.Damage, whose Hook.ShouldDie / Hook.AfterPreventingDeath pass runs over RunState.IterateHookListeners (RunState.cs:545-596), which yields the POTION BELT outside combat; RunState.lose_hp (run.py:294-302) just subtracts
guards.issue: MECHANISM EV-1, one verdict at all 18 lose_hp sites (rule 3). Fairy in a Bottle (FairyInABottle.cs:33-45: ShouldDie false for its owner, AfterPreventingDeath heals to max(MaxHp*0.3, 1)) IS ported (potions.py:1222-1250) and IS in the reward pool (potion_pools.py:49), but the sim's copy returns early when `self.combat is None` (potions.py:1246-1248) and is only registered as a listener by CombatState (combat.py:164-166), so it is inert during an event. EXECUTED (`py tools/audit/event_probes.py lethal`): a run at 5 HP holding a belt Fairy that loses 15 HP ends DEAD at hp=-10 with the Fairy still in the belt; the game ends alive at 24 HP with the Fairy consumed. LIVE -- both sides ported and reachable, and the divergence ends the run. Secondary: run.lose_hp does not clamp at 0 either, so the sim carries negative HP.

guards.maps_to: events/this_or_that.py:37-40 lose_hp then gain_gold, same order. The order is observable because a relic that reads HP could gate the gold (none ported does), and because a lethal PLAIN in the game would end the run before the gold is awarded.

events/this_or_that.py:42-46 run.pull_relic_from_front() + run.add_relic(), then run.add_card(make_card('clumsy')). Three checks. (1) STREAM: the one-argument PullNextRelicFromFront(player) rolls its rarity on player.PlayerRng.Rewards (RelicFactory.cs:28, :82), and run.pull_relic_from_front defaults rarity_rng to run.rewards_rng (run.py:588-589), which is player_rng.rewards under a parity rng_set (run.py:271-274) -- the correct stream, so this is NOT an EV-3 site (the batch-3-vs-4 self-correction in the stream report settles this). (2) VERB: CardPileCmd.AddCurseToDeck<T> is a thin wrapper over AddCursesToDeck, which type-asserts Curse and then calls the ordinary `Add(card, PileType.Deck)` (CardPileCmd.cs:1037-1056) -- so run.add_card, which runs the same deck-entry hook, is the right port and no egg relic matches a Curse in either build. (3) ORDER: relic before curse in both, which matters -- Darkstone Periapt gains Max HP on a Curse entering the deck (run.py:349-352 after_card_added_to_deck), so pulling it here and then adding Clumsy triggers it, and the reverse order would not. The sim's `if relic is not None` guard is the empty-grab-bag case, where the C# would dereference null.

guards.what: EV-3: ThisOrThat.CalculateVars' NextInt(41, 69) gold roll (events/this_or_that.py:29). EXECUTED (`py tools/audit/event_probes_b.py rng5b`): this_or_that has no event_rng branch at all rolls on the sim's shared run RNG (`self.rng`) where C# rolls on the per-event `base.Rng`
guards.issue: MECHANISM EV-3, one verdict at every site (rule 3). Each C# EventModel gets its own Rng seeded from the run seed + event id, and the sim already models it: Event.__init__ builds `self.event_rng` from make_event_rng(seed, ID) for string-seeded runs (events/base.py:84-88), and 6 modules branch on it. EXECUTED (`py tools/audit/event_probes.py eventrng`): 28 of the 34 event modules that roll anything roll ONLY on `self.rng`. LIVE for the parity path that the conformance harness grades -- a shared-rng draw both takes a number the game never takes off that stream and fails to advance the event stream, desyncing the rest of the run. In legacy (RL) mode both are the same random.Random, so the observable is parity-only -- which is an exercised sim mode, not an unreachable one.
